summary_text: This shopper is a staple-driven household buyer with strong, high-confidence brand loyalty in core dairy, bakery, and pantry categories, while maintaining flexible, need-based purchasing for fresh produce and exploratory behavior in snack categories. The profile is defined by a consistent preference for specific branded items—such as Naturbaked bread, Mother Dairy curd, Amul milk, and Del Monte canned goods—purchased repeatedly across multiple months. Fresh vegetables and fruits are bought with high flexibility, dominated by recurring cauliflower purchases but lacking stable brand or variety preferences. The shopper exhibits low substitution tolerance for their core branded staples but shows openness to variety in snacks and condiments. Shopping timing is highly flexible across all dayparts and days, indicating that purchases are driven by immediate household replenishment needs rather than rigid daily routines.

retrieval_text: The user demonstrates high-confidence, stable brand loyalty for Naturbaked whole wheat bread (17+ dates), Mother Dairy curd (14+ dates), Amul milk (multiple months), Del Monte baked beans (11 dates), and Amul cheese/paneer. These core staples are purchased repeatedly across February–July 2026, indicating a strong preference for these specific brands over competitors. In contrast, fresh vegetables show a stable preference for Cauliflower (400-600g) but no brand loyalty, while fruits and snacks exhibit exploratory behavior with no stable preferences. The user shops flexibly across all dayparts and days, with no dominant timing routine. A medium-confidence relationship exists between Curd Yogurt and Vegetables, which are often bought together. The shopper prefers small-format, single-serve, or standard household pack sizes (e.g., 500ml milk, 200g curd, 1kg sugar) and shows low tendency for large multi-quantity baskets, suggesting frequent, need-based replenishment of daily essentials.
